[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Merge Intervals** [LC 56 · Merge Intervals](https://leetcode.com/problems/merge-intervals/){difficulty="Medium"}

Overlap is a *pairwise* relation, so the definition of the answer is "$O(n^2)$" — but sorting by start collapses it. Once the intervals are ordered left-to-right, any interval that overlaps the current block must have its start inside the block, so a single running `cur_end` variable decides everything: extend or open new. This is @sec-srt's "sort first" purchase spent on the *merge* relation. The subtle bug that catches almost everyone is comparing an interval to the *previous original* end instead of the *current block* end; nested intervals like $[1,10],[2,3],[4,5]$ then shrink the block incorrectly.

[Solved in full in @sec-int-p1-a.]{.card-link}

:::
